questions.question: Seven boxes M, N, O, P, Q, R and S are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. Only two boxes are kept below S. Only one box is kept above Q. Only one box is kept between Q and P. R is kept immediately above N. O is kept at some place below M. How many boxes are kept between M and R?
questions.questionHtml: Seven boxes M, N, O, P, Q, R and S are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. Only two boxes are kept below S. Only one box is kept above Q. Only one box is kept between Q and P. R is kept immediately above N. O is kept at some place below M. How many boxes are kept between M and R?
questions.solution:
Given:

We are taking Top = 1, Bottom = 7.

“Two boxes below S” → S must be at position 5.

“Only one box above Q” → Q must be at position 2.

“Only one box between Q and P” → P = 4.

“R immediately above N” → R = 6, N = 7.

“O is below M” → M = 1, O = 3.

Final order (Top → Bottom):

1    M

2    Q

3    O

4    P

5    S

6    R

7    N

Boxes between M (1) and R (6) = positions 2, 3, 4, 5 → 4 boxes

Hence, the correct answer is 4

Only I and II are implicit.

questions.question: Which of the following part of the Himalayas located between Kali and Teesta rivers?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following part of the Himalayas located between Kali and Teesta rivers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nepal Himalayas.

The Himalayas have been divided on the basis of regions from west to east. These divisions have been demarcated by river valleys.

The Nepal Himalayas is located between Kali and Teesta rivers.

Nepal Himalayas:

  • Nepal Himalayas, east-central section and highest part of the Himalayan mountain ranges in south-central Asia
  • It extending some 500 miles (800 km) from the Kali River east to the Tista River.
  • The Great Himalaya range attains maximum height in this portion.
  • Some of the world-famous peaks Mt. Everest, Kanchenjunga, Makalu, Annapurna, Gosainthan, and Dhaulagiri are located here.
  • The Lesser Himalaya is known as Mahabharat Lekh in this region.
  • The range is crossed by rivers like Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi, etc.
  • In between the Great and the Lesser Himalayas, there are Kathmandu and Pokhra lacustrine valleys (previously, they were lakes).
  • The Shiwalik range comes very close to the lesser Himalaya towards the east and is almost non-existent beyond Narayani (Gandak)
 

Parts of Himalaya Located between

Punjab/Kashmir Himalayas
  • The part of the Himalayas lies between the Indus River and the Satluj River.

Kumaon Himalayas
  • The part of the Himalayas that lies between Satluj River and Kali River.

Nepal Himalayas
  • The part of the Himalayas that lies between the Kali River and Teesta River.

Assam Himalayas
  • The part of the Himalayas that lies between the Teesta River and Dihang River.

Purvanchal/Eastern Himalayas
  • The part of the Himalayas that lies beyond Dihang River valley.
  • Here the Himalayas bend sharply towards the south and spread along Indo-Myanmar Border.

questions.question: In which of the following river valleys in India is the deposit of coal the largest?

questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is The Damodar.

Key Points

questions.questionHtml: <span '="">Which type of spherical mirror is used by dentists to see a large image of the teeth of patients?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Concave mirror

Key Points
  • A Concave mirror is the type of spherical mirror used by dentists to see a large (magnified) image of a patient's teeth.
  • The core logic lies in the image formation properties of a concave mirror: when an object is placed very close to the mirror (between the pole and the principal focus), the resulting image is virtual, erect, and magnified.
  • Plane mirrors are incorrect because they produce an image that is the same size as the object, providing no magnification for detailed dental work.
  • Convex mirrors are incorrect because they always produce a diminished (smaller) image, which would make it harder for a dentist to see details.
  • Bifocal mirrors is not a standard term in optics; bifocal lenses are used in spectacles to correct vision, not for magnification in dental tools.
Additional Information
  • Concave mirrors are also widely used in shaving mirrors and makeup mirrors to provide a clear, enlarged view of the face.
  • They are used in torches, searchlights, and vehicle headlights to produce a powerful parallel beam of light when the light source is placed at the focus.
  • Convex mirrors are commonly used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles because they give a wider field of view, allowing drivers to see a large area of traffic behind them.
  • A spherical mirror whose reflecting surface is curved inwards (towards the center of the sphere) is a concave mirror, while one curved outwards is a convex mirror.

questions.question: "Eutrophication" in aquatic ecosystems like Kerala's backwaters is primarily driven by an excess of which nutrients?
questions.questionHtml: "Eutrophication" in aquatic ecosystems like Kerala's backwaters is primarily driven by an excess of which nutrients?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nitrogen and Phosphorus.

Key Points

  • Eutrophication is a process where a body of water becomes overly enriched with minerals and nutrients that induce excessive growth of algae.
  • This phenomenon is primarily driven by the accumulation of Nitrogen and Phosphorus in the aquatic ecosystem. These nutrients act as fertilizers for aquatic plants and microscopic organisms. Hence, the statement regarding Nitrogen and Phosphorus is correct.
  • The presence of these nutrients leads to Algal Blooms, which create a dense layer on the water surface, preventing sunlight from penetrating deeper layers of the water body.
  • As the algae die, microorganisms like bacteria decompose them, a process that consumes large quantities of Dissolved Oxygen (DO). This leads to a state of hypoxia, where oxygen levels are too low to support fish and other aquatic life.

Additional Information

  • Sources of Nutrients: In India, particularly in Kerala's backwaters, the high concentration of Nitrogen and Phosphorus is attributed to agricultural runoff from the Kuttanad region, where chemical fertilizers are heavily used in paddy cultivation.
  • Types of Eutrophication:
    • Natural Eutrophication: A slow, geological process where nutrients accumulate over centuries as a lake ages.
    • Cultural Eutrophication: A rapid, human-induced process caused by urbanization, industrial waste, and domestic sewage.
  • Impact on Kerala: The Vembanad Lake, a designated Ramsar Site in Kerala, has suffered significantly from eutrophication, leading to the proliferation of water hyacinths and a decline in traditional shrimp and fish farming.
  • Consequences: Beyond hypoxia, eutrophication can lead to the production of toxins by certain algae (cyanobacteria), which can contaminate drinking water and harm public health.

Important Points

  • Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD): This is a crucial numerical value used to measure water pollution. During eutrophication, the BOD increases significantly because more oxygen is needed by aerobic bacteria to break down the excess organic matter.
  • Limiting Nutrients: In most freshwater ecosystems, Phosphorus is the primary limiting nutrient, meaning its addition has the most immediate impact on algal growth. In marine or brackish waters, Nitrogen often plays this role.
  • Regulatory Framework: The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) in India monitors nutrient levels under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, to mitigate the degradation of sensitive aquatic ecosystems.
  • Prevention: Methods to control eutrophication include the diversion of sewage, reducing the use of phosphate-based detergents, and creating riparian buffer zones to filter agricultural runoff before it reaches the water.

questions.question: If the area of a sector is 58.5 cm 2 , then find its perimeter if the radius of the circle is 6.5 cm.
questions.questionHtml: If the area of a sector is 58.5 cm<sup>2</sup>, then find its perimeter if the radius of the circle is 6.5 cm.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Arc Length (l) = (2 × Area) ÷ Radius

l = (2 × 58.5) ÷ 6.5 = 117 ÷ 6.5 = 18 cm

Perimeter of Sector = l + 2r

Perimeter = 18 + 2 × 6.5 = 18 + 13 = 31 cm

∴ The correct answer is 31 cm.

Alternate Method

Given: Area of sector = 58.5 cm2, Radius (r) = 6.5 cm.

Formula Used: Area = (1/2) × r × l and Perimeter = l + 2r

⇒ Area = (1/2) × r × l

⇒ 58.5 = (1/2) × 6.5 × l

⇒ l = (58.5 × 2) ÷ 6.5

⇒ l = 117 ÷ 6.5 = 18 cm

⇒ Perimeter = l + 2r

⇒ Perimeter = 18 + 2 × 6.5

⇒ Perimeter = 18 + 13 = 31 cm

∴ The correct answer is 31 cm.

Additional Information

Area of Sector (using angle)

Area = (θ/360°) × πr2, where θ is the central angle in degrees.

Length of Arc

Arc length (l) = (θ/360°) × 2πr, representing the curved boundary of the sector.

Relation between Area and Arc Length

Area = (Arc length × Radius) ÷ 2. This is useful when the angle θ is unknown.

Perimeter of Sector

Perimeter = Length of Arc + 2 × Radius. It includes both the curved boundary and the two straight radii.

questions.question: A car covered 240 km in 5 h. If it travels with half of its usual speed, then how much more time will be taken to cover the same distance?
questions.questionHtml: A car covered 240 km in 5 h. If it travels with half of its usual speed, then how much more time will be taken to cover the same distance?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When Distance is constant, Speed is inversely proportional to Time (S ∝ 1/T).

Speed ratio (Original : New) = 1 : 1/2 = 2 : 1.

Time ratio (Original : New) = Inverse of speed ratio = 1 : 2.

Original time (1 unit) = 5 h.

More time taken = New time − Original time = 2 units − 1 unit = 1 unit.

Value of 1 unit = 5 h.

∴ The correct answer is 5 h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total Distance = 240 km

Initial Time = 5 h

Formula Used:

Speed = Distance ÷ Time | Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Calculations:

⇒ Usual Speed = 240 ÷ 5 = 48 kmph

⇒ New Speed = 48 ÷ 2 = 24 kmph

⇒ New Time taken = 240 ÷ 24 = 10 h

⇒ Extra time = New Time − Initial Time

⇒ Extra time = 10 − 5 = 5 h

∴ The correct answer is 5 h.

Additional Information

Speed-Time Relationship

When distance is fixed, if the speed is multiplied by a factor n, the time is multiplied by 1/n.

Unit Conversion

To convert Speed from kmph to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to kmph, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

If a journey is divided into two equal distances with speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

questions.questionHtml: If a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2 </sup>+ c<sup>2</sup> = ab + bc + ac, then find the value of a<sup>3</sup> + b<sup>3</sup> + c<sup>3</sup>.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For real numbers, the condition a2 + b2 + c2 = ab + bc + ac is satisfied only when a = b = c.

Let a = b = c = 1. Then, 12 + 12 + 12 = 1×1 + 1×1 + 1×1 ⇒ 3 = 3.

Substitute these values into the required expression: a3 + b3 + c3 = 13 + 13 + 13 = 3.

Among the options, 3abc = 3 × 1 × 1 × 1 = 3, which matches the result.

∴ The correct answer is 3abc.

Alternate Method

Given: a2 + b2 + c2 = ab + bc + ac

Formula Used: a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a2 + b2 + c2 − ab − bc − ac)

⇒ a2 + b2 + c2 − ab − bc − ac = 0

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = (a + b + c) × (a2 + b2 + c2 − ab − bc − ac)

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = (a + b + c) × 0

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = 0

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 = 3abc

∴ The correct answer is 3abc.

Additional Information

Cubic Algebra Identity

The general expansion is a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a2 + b2 + c2 − ab − bc − ac).

Special Conditional Case

If a + b + c = 0, then the entire product on the right side becomes zero, resulting in a3 + b3 + c3 = 3abc.

Equality Condition for Squares

The expression a2 + b2 + c2 − ab − bc − ac can be rewritten as 1/2[(a − b)2 + (b − c)2 + (c − a)2]. For real numbers, this is 0 only when a = b = c.

questions.question: A 6 cm long chord subtends an angle of 60° at the center of the circle. If the length of another chord of the same circle is 6√3 cm, then find the measure of the angle subtended by the chord at the center of the circle.

questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If a chord subtends 60° at the center, the triangle formed is equilateral → Radius (r) = Chord = 6 cm.

Use Chord formula: Length = 2 × r × sin(θ/2)

6√3 = 2 × 6 × sin(θ/2) ⇒ sin(θ/2) = √3 / 2

Since sin(60°) = √3 / 2, then θ/2 = 60° ⇒ θ = 120°.

∴ The correct answer is 120°.

Alternate Method

Given:

A chord of length 6 cm subtends an angle of 60° at the center of a circle. If the length of another chord of the same circle is 6√3 cm.

Calculation:

In ΔAOM,

AM = AB/2 = 6/2 = 3 cm

∠AOM = ∠AOB/2 = 60/2 = 30°

Therefore, ∠OAM = 180 - 30 - 90 = 60°

Cos60 = b/h = \(\dfrac{3}{r}\)

⇒ \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) = \(\dfrac{3}{r}\)

⇒ r = 6

Therefore, in ΔPON,

PN = PQ/2 = 6√3/2 = 3√3 cm

OP = r = 6 cm

Sinθ1 = \(\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{6}\)

⇒ Sinθ1 = \(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\)

⇒ Sinθ1 = Sin60°

⇒ θ1 = 60°

∠POQ = 2θ1 = 2 × 60° = 120°

∴ Option (1) is the correct answer.

Additional Information

Chord Length Formula

The length of a chord subtending an angle θ at the center of a circle with radius r is given by L = 2r sin(θ/2).

Equilateral Triangle Property

A chord that subtends a 60° angle at the center always forms an equilateral triangle with the two radii, meaning the chord length equals the radius.

Angle Subtended at Circumference

The angle subtended by a chord at the center is exactly twice the angle subtended by it at any point on the major arc of the circumference.

questions.question: If 6cotθ = 5, then find the value of \(\frac{6cos \theta + sin\theta }{6cos \theta - 4 sin\theta}\) .

Shortcut Trick

Divide the numerator and the denominator of the given expression by sinθ.

The expression (6cosθ + sinθ) ÷ (6cosθ − 4sinθ) becomes (6cotθ + 1) ÷ (6cotθ − 4).

Substitute the given value 6cotθ = 5 directly into the simplified expression.

⇒ (5 + 1) ÷ (5 − 4)

⇒ 6 ÷ 1 = 6

∴ The correct answer is 6.

Alternate Method

Given:

6cotθ = 5

Formula Used:

cotθ = cosθ ÷ sinθ

Calculations:

⇒ cotθ = 5 ÷ 6

⇒ cosθ ÷ sinθ = 5 ÷ 6

Since the degree of the given trigonometric expression is homogeneous (equal degrees in both numerator and denominator), we can directly substitute the ratio values by taking cosθ = 5k and sinθ = 6k.

Given expression: (6cosθ + sinθ) ÷ (6cosθ − 4sinθ)

⇒ [(6 × 5k) + 6k] ÷ [(6 × 5k) − (4 × 6k)]

⇒ (30k + 6k) ÷ (30k − 24k)

⇒ 36k ÷ 6k

⇒ 6

∴ The correct answer is 6.

Additional Information

Ratio Substitution in Trigonometry

When evaluating an expression with equal degrees of sine and cosine in the numerator and denominator, direct ratio values can be substituted instead of calculating the exact fundamental trigonometric values.

Key Trigonometric Ratios

tanθ = sinθ ÷ cosθ | cotθ = cosθ ÷ sinθ

Pythagorean Identities

sin2θ + cos2θ = 1 | 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ | 1 + cot2θ = cosec2θ

questions.question: A man travelled from A to B at a speed of 10 m/sec, and returned to A from B at a speed of x km/h. If his average speed is 45 km/h, then what is the value of x ?
questions.questionHtml: A man travelled from A to B at a speed of 10 m/sec, and returned to A from B at a speed of x km/h. If his average speed is 45 km/h, then what is the value of x ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Convert the forward speed from m/s to km/h: S1 = 10 × (18 / 5) = 36 km/h.

For equal travel distances, the average speed formula is: (2 × S1 × S2) / (S1 + S2).

⇒ 45 = (2 × 36 × x) / (36 + x)

⇒ 45 × (36 + x) = 72x

⇒ 1620 + 45x = 72x ⇒ 27x = 1620 ⇒ x = 60

∴ The correct answer is x = 60.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed from A to B (S1) = 10 m/sec

Speed from B to A (S2) = x km/h

Average Speed for the whole journey = 45 km/h

Formula Used:

Average Speed = (2 × S1 × S2) / (S1 + S2)

Calculations:

⇒ First, we must equalize the units. Convert S1 from m/sec to km/h.

⇒ S1 = 10 × (18 / 5) = 36 km/h

⇒ Now, substitute the known values into the average speed formula:

⇒ 45 = (2 × 36 × x) / (36 + x)

⇒ 45 = 72x / (36 + x)

⇒ 45 × (36 + x) = 72x

⇒ 1620 + 45x = 72x

⇒ 72x − 45x = 1620

⇒ 27x = 1620

⇒ x = 1620 ÷ 27 = 60

∴ The correct answer is x = 60.

Additional Information

Unit Conversion for Speed

To directly convert speed given in m/s to km/h, multiply the value by 18/5. Conversely, to convert from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18.

Average Speed for Equal Distances

When an individual travels back and forth between two points (equal distances) at speeds S1 and S2, the effective average speed for the entire trip is strictly calculated using the harmonic mean: (2 × S1 × S2) / (S1 + S2).

Average Speed General Formula

If distances travelled are different, the standard average speed formula should be used: Total Distance Covered ÷ Total Time Taken.

questions.question: A student scored 20% less and another student scored 25% more than the average marks of the class. What is the ratio of the 1st student to the average score of the student to the another student?
questions.questionHtml: A student scored 20% less and another student scored 25% more than the average marks of the class. What is the ratio of the 1st student to the average score of the student to the another student?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the average marks of the class be 100 units.

Score of 1st student = 100 − 20 = 80 units.

Score of 2nd student = 100 + 25 = 125 units.

Required Ratio = 80 : 100 : 125.

Simplifying by dividing each part by 5: 16 : 20 : 25.

∴ The correct answer is 16 : 20 : 25.

Alternate Method

Given:

Score of 1st student = 20% less than Average.

Score of 2nd student = 25% more than Average.

Calculations:

⇒ Let the average marks of the class be x.

⇒ Marks of 1st student = x − (20/100) × x = x − 0.2x = 0.8x.

⇒ Marks of 2nd student = x + (25/100) × x = x + 0.25x = 1.25x.

⇒ Required Ratio = (Score of 1st student) : (Average Marks) : (Score of 2nd student)

⇒ Required Ratio = 0.8x : x : 1.25x

⇒ Required Ratio = 0.8 : 1 : 1.25

⇒ To remove decimals, multiply by 100: 80 : 100 : 125.

⇒ Dividing by the common factor 5: (80÷5) : (100÷5) : (125÷5).

⇒ Required Ratio = 16 : 20 : 25.

∴ The correct answer is 16 : 20 : 25.

Additional Information

Percentage and Base Value

When comparing values using percentages, it is standard practice to assume the reference value (base) as 100 for simplicity.

Simplifying Ratios

A ratio a : b : c can be simplified by dividing all terms by their Highest Common Factor (HCF) or multiplying them by the same non-zero number to eliminate decimals or fractions.

Percentage Change Formula

Increase = Base × (1 + Rate/100) and Decrease = Base × (1 − Rate/100).

Age Ratio After 'n' Years

If the current ratio is a:b, then after 'n' years the ages will be (ak + n) and (bk + n). The difference between ages always remains constant.

Proportionality Rule

If a:b = c:d, then product of extremes (a × d) is always equal to the product of means (b × c).

questions.question: Ramu's father told Ramu to find the smallest number which is a perfect square and is also divisible by 12, 18, 24, and 27.
questions.questionHtml: Ramu's father told Ramu to find the smallest number which is a perfect square and is also divisible by 12, 18, 24, and 27.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Find the LCM of 12, 18, 24, and 27 first.

LCM(12, 18, 24, 27) = 216.

Prime factorize 216: 216 = 23 × 33.

To make it a perfect square, multiply by the missing factors to make powers even: 216 × (2 × 3) = 1296.

Check options: 1296 is the only perfect square (362) divisible by all given numbers.

∴ The correct answer is 1296.

Alternate Method

Given numbers: 12, 18, 24, 27

Formula used: LCM × (unpaired prime factors) = Smallest Perfect Square

Perform prime factorization of each number:

⇒ 12 = 22 × 31

⇒ 18 = 21 × 32

⇒ 24 = 23 × 31

⇒ 27 = 33

⇒ LCM = 23 × 33 = 8 × 27 = 216

⇒ To be a perfect square, each prime factor must have an even exponent.

⇒ Required Number = 23+1 × 33+1 = 24 × 34

⇒ Required Number = 16 × 81 = 1296

∴ The correct answer is 1296.

Additional Information

Perfect Square Property

A number is a perfect square if and only if all the exponents in its prime factorization are even integers.

LCM of Numbers

The Least Common Multiple (LCM) is the smallest positive integer that is divisible by each of the given numbers. To find LCM, take the highest power of each prime factor present in the numbers.

Smallest Multiple as a Square

To find the smallest square multiple of a set of numbers, first find their LCM and then multiply it by the minimum required prime factors to make all exponents even.

questions.question: A retailer buys a cell phone at a discount of 15% and sells it for Rs. 5865. Thus he makes a profit of 15%. The discount is?
questions.questionHtml: A retailer buys a cell phone at a discount of 15% and sells it for Rs. 5865. Thus he makes a profit of 15%. The discount is?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio MP : CP = 100 : 85 = 20 : 17

Ratio CP : SP = 100 : 115 = 20 : 23

Merged MP : CP : SP = (20×20) : (17×20) : (17×23) = 400 : 340 : 391

Given SP 391 units = ₹5865 → 1 unit = ₹15

Discount = MP − CP = 400 − 340 = 60 units = 60 × 15 = ₹900

∴ The correct answer is ₹900.

Alternate Method

Given:

Selling Price (SP) = ₹5865

Profit Percentage = 15%

Purchase Discount Percentage = 15%

Formula Used:

Cost Price (CP) = SP × 100 / (100 + Profit %)

Marked Price (MP) = CP × 100 / (100 − Discount %)

Calculations:

⇒ CP = 5865 × 100 / (100 + 15)

⇒ CP = 5865 × 100 / 115

⇒ CP = ₹5100

⇒ Let the Marked Price be MP.

⇒ Retailer gets 15% discount on MP, so CP = 85% of MP.

⇒ 5100 = (85 / 100) × MP

⇒ MP = (5100 × 100) / 85

⇒ MP = ₹6000

⇒ Discount Amount = MP − CP = 6000 − 5100

⇒ Discount Amount = ₹900

∴ The correct answer is ₹900.

Additional Information

Relationship between CP and MP

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price can be expressed as MP / CP = (100 + Profit %) / (100 − Discount %).

Discount and Profit

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP), while Profit or Loss is calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the single equivalent discount is (a + b − ab/100)%.

questions.question: When the elevation of the sun changes from 45º to 30º, the shadow of the tower changes by 20 m. Find the height of the tower.
questions.questionHtml: When the elevation of the sun changes from 45º to 30º, the shadow of the tower changes by 20 m. Find the height of the tower.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Distance (d) between two shadow points is given by: d = h(cot θ2 − cot θ1)

Given, d = 20 m, θ1 = 45°, and θ2 = 30°

⇒ 20 = h(cot 30° − cot 45°) = h(√3 − 1)

⇒ h = 20 ÷ (√3 − 1)

⇒ h = [20(√3 + 1)] ÷ 2 = 10(√3 + 1) m

∴ The correct answer is 10(√3 + 1) m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Change in sun's elevation = 45° to 30°

Change in length of shadow (CD) = 20 m

Let AB = h be the height of the tower and BC = x be the initial shadow length.

Calculations:

In right-angled ΔABC,

⇒ tan 45° = AB ÷ BC

⇒ 1 = h ÷ x

⇒ x = h

In right-angled ΔABD,

⇒ tan 30° = AB ÷ BD

⇒ 1 ÷ √3 = h ÷ (x + 20)

⇒ x + 20 = h√3

Substitute x = h into the equation:

⇒ h + 20 = h√3

⇒ h√3 − h = 20

⇒ h(√3 − 1) = 20

⇒ h = 20 ÷ (√3 − 1)

Rationalising the denominator by multiplying the numerator and denominator by (√3 + 1):

⇒ h = [20 × (√3 + 1)] ÷ [(√3 − 1)(√3 + 1)]

⇒ h = 20(√3 + 1) ÷ (3 − 1)

⇒ h = 20(√3 + 1) ÷ 2

⇒ h = 10(√3 + 1) m

∴ The correct answer is 10(√3 + 1) m.

Additional Information

Angle of Elevation

It is the angle formed between the horizontal line of sight and the object when the observer looks upwards.

Important Trigonometric Values

For height and distance problems, remember these values: tan 30° = 1 ÷ √3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3.

Rationalisation

To remove surds from the denominator like (a − √b), multiply both numerator and denominator by its conjugate (a + √b) to create a rational base.
